title: Git range capture in plan and close
objective: Every sprint planned and closed with this version records a deterministic, checkpoint-verifiable git range (branch, start commit, end commit, dirty flag) in the scope ledger, while every existing scope and checkpoint keeps validating and re-deriving unchanged.

phases.title: Data contract and read-only git capture
phases.objective: Define the optional git blocks with validation and a non-throwing read-only git capture helper.

Create scripts/check-sprint-git-traceability.mjs (temp data under ~/.cache/kyro-tmp or os.tmpdir) with contract cases, add npm script check:sprint-git-traceability, include it in the aggregate npm run check, and add it to the checkpoints rule in .agents/kyro/validation.json.
tasks.context: Findings 01 and 05. tasks.title: Implement a non-throwing read-only git capture helper
tasks.description: Create src/cli/core/git-capture.ts exporting functions that, for a given cwd, return the HEAD commit and branch (null when detached), or null when not a repository, git is missing, HEAD is unborn, or any git call fails; and report whether tracked or untracked non-ignored files outside .agents/kyro/ have uncommitted changes. Use execFileSync('git', [...args]) with array arguments and no shell, as in src/cli/core/git-trackability.ts. The helper performs no writes and never throws.
tasks.context: Findings 01, 05. R4: capture never blocks planning or closing. R5: dirty excludes .agents/kyro/ because the close itself writes there, and excludes gitignored files. Must work on Windows (no shell quoting, no POSIX-only paths). Build the check cases with real temporary git repositories.
acceptance_criteria: In temporary repositories the helper returns the correct commit and branch for a normal branch, branch null for detached HEAD, and null for a non-repository directory and for a repository with no commits — proven by npm run check:sprint-git-traceability.
Dirty is false when only .agents/kyro/ files or ignored files changed, and true for a modified tracked file and for a new untracked non-ignored file — proven by the same check.
No call path throws when git is unavailable or fails (simulated with an invalid cwd), and npm run build plus npm run check:git-trackability pass.

evidence.summary: Added src/cli/core/git-capture.ts: readGitHead (HEAD commit + branch, null branch when detached), hasUncommittedChangesOutsideKyro (porcelain -z, untracked included, ignored excluded, excludes the workspace's own .agents/kyro/ using rev-parse --show-prefix), captureSprintGitStart and captureSprintGitEnd. execFileSync with array args, no shell, 10s timeout; every function returns null instead of throwing (non-repo, missing git, unborn HEAD, any failure).

Mutation: KYRO_DIR changed in dist => check fails on the two exclusion cases; restored => pass

tasks.title: Freeze the end commit in close inputs and derive the ledger range
tasks.description: In buildClosePlan's fresh path, capture { branch, endCommit, dirty } before any write and set it as close.git when available. retryCloseInputs must copy checkpoint.close.git verbatim so assertMatchingCloseInputs keeps matching. deriveSprintCloseTransitionWithPolicy adds ledger git = { branch: close.git.branch, startCommit: beforeClose.activeSprint.git?.startCommit ?? null, endCommit, dirty } only when close.git exists. Render a 'Git' section in the archive narrative when present. When dirty is true, the CLI close prints a warning that uncommitted changes are outside the sprint range, and the MCP close result exposes the captured git data.
tasks.context: Finding 01; R2, R3, R5. Checkpoint verification re-derives intendedAfterClose from frozen inputs and compares canonically (sprint-close.ts:282-300); any ledger git data not derived from frozen inputs breaks verification. A legacy checkpoint without close.git must derive exactly as today. Never read HEAD on the retry/resume path.
acceptance_criteria: Closing a sprint in a temporary repository records ledger git with the planned startCommit, endCommit equal to HEAD before the close, the branch, and dirty — and the new checkpoint re-derives identically — proven by npm run check:sprint-git-traceability.
After an interrupted close and a new commit, retrying the close keeps the original endCommit and raises no CHECKPOINT_CONFLICT — proven by the same check.

A close of a sprint without activeSprint.git records startCommit null; a legacy checkpoint without close.git still verifies and re-derives byte-identically — proven by npm run check:lossless-checkpoints, npm run check:close-policy-compatibility, and npm run check:sprint-git-traceability.
npm run build, npm run check:close-handoff, npm run check:lifecycle-replay, and npm run check:mcp pass.

evidence.summary: buildClosePlan fresh path freezes captureSprintGitEnd() as close.git before any write; retryCloseInputs copies checkpoint.close.git so retries never re-read HEAD; deriveSprintCloseTransitionWithPolicy adds ledger.git {branch, startCommit from beforeClose.activeSprint.git or null, endCommit, dirty} only when close.git exists. Narrative gets a 'Git range' section; CLI prints the range (or 'not recorded') and a dirty warning; MCP applied result exposes git. Fix found here: the state-writer lock directory at the workspace root is held during close and is not gitignored at root, so every close read dirty=true; hasUncommittedChangesOutsideKyro (T1.2 file) now also excludes STATE_WRITER_LOCK (exported from state-writer-lock.ts).
validation: npm run check:sprint-git-traceability: pass (S3 real close in temp repo: ledger git = main, planned startCommit, endCommit = HEAD before close, dirty false; checkpoint re-derives with zero integrity issues; narrative has the range. S7 all 28 repo checkpoints still re-derive with zero integrity issues)

emergentTasks.title: Harden git capture: lock-free status, accurate failure reasons, reclaim dirs, Windows CI
emergentTasks.description: Run git status with --no-optional-locks so capture never rewrites .git/index; when HEAD resolves but status fails or times out, report that specific reason instead of 'not a git repository' (close output and narrative-independent CLI message), keeping the end commit omitted per R4; exclude every root path starting with the state-writer lock name (including .kyro-state-writer.lock.reclaim-* leftovers) from the dirty check; move printGitRange above renderNarrative's JSDoc with its own doc; add npm run check:sprint-git-traceability to the Windows CI job.
emergentTasks.context: Required by kyro qa: minors 1, 2, 3, 4, 5. Evidence must also complete the T1.5 per-writer audit list (minor 6: clarify, debt, rule, repair/integrity-plan, remediation/certification-plan, checkpoints/lifecycle-state).
